title: A2UI Express separates UI generation from rendering
dek: Google introduces a compact inference format that compiles into validated A2UI messages, reducing model output while keeping rendering under client control.
evidence: Google vendor measurements; independent replication pending
takeaway: Prototype A2UI Express against direct JSON on representative financial workflows. Measure end-to-end latency, valid render rate, authorization checks and correction cost before selecting a generation format.

sections.title: Mechanism

bullets.detail: The client supplies a catalog of allowed UI components. The agent proposes a component tree; the client renders validated structures rather than executing model-generated interface code.
Catalog constraints restrict UI structures, not the truth of displayed values or permission to execute actions. Server-side entitlements and data provenance remain separate controls.

example.takeaway: Express replaces repeated field names with short assignments. The SDK compiles them into A2UI JSON for the same renderer.

sections.title: Performance claims

bullets.detail: Google reports up to 3× fewer output tokens and up to 3× lower latency versus Direct JSON; its comparison spans 51 tasks with gemini-3.5-flash under different thinking settings.
Direct JSON can stream chunks; Express waits for the full response before compilation. Faster completion does not guarantee earlier first useful render.

Google separately cites up to 80× faster layout decisions with Jev. An 11-prompt demonstration reported 92–298 ms component trees and 0.8–1.7 s complete screens; this is not an independent Express comparison.

sections.title: What to verify

bullets.detail: Published figures are vendor measurements, not independently replicated production latency, cost, correctness, or security results. Jev's format is not yet included in the cited SDKs.
Run 50–100 representative document, market-data, alert, and research tasks with the same model, catalog, and backend; compare Direct JSON with Express.

Measure p50/p95 end-to-end time, first useful render, token cost, valid renders, missing fields, retries, and denied-action behavior. Only promote when correctness and authorization meet baseline thresholds.
